obsidian.$description: Obsidian — Page canvas, footer background, deepest surface — near-black with the faintest blue undertone

onyx.$description: Onyx — Card surface, secondary backdrop — one step deeper than the page for visual weight

carbon.$description: Carbon — Elevated panels, subtle UI fills — the first clearly lighter step in the surface stack

graphite.$description: Graphite — Borders, dividers, icon containers, slider controls — the hairline color that defines structure

slate.$description: Slate — Secondary borders, muted icon strokes, subtle dividers between content blocks

smoke.$description: Smoke — Tertiary borders, inactive nav items — barely visible structural lines

ash.$description: Ash — Muted body text, placeholder content, secondary metadata

steel.$description: Steel — Button borders, icon strokes, secondary text, ghost button outlines

fog.$description: Fog — Nav text, body descriptions, helper text — the workhorse readable gray

mist.$description: Mist — Subdued body copy, supplementary text, less-emphasized paragraphs

silver.$description: Silver — Light body text, medium-emphasis paragraphs, secondary headings

bone.$description: Bone — High-emphasis body text, dense data labels, the default text tone across most UI

paper-white.$description: Paper White — Primary action button fill, headings, nav active state — the highest contrast color, reserved for elements that must command attention

copper.$description: Copper — Category labels, editorial links, warm accent punctuation — the only chromatic color, used sparingly to mark curated content and category tags

gilded-gradient.$description: Gilded Gradient — Chart line stroke, financial data visualization accent — a warm gold-to-cream gradient that brings the only color energy to data displays

ivy-presto.$description: Display and heading serif — used exclusively for hero headlines and section titles at 28px and above. The high-contrast didone strokes with hairline serifs create editorial luxury; the slight 0.01em positive tracking is unusual and gives the type a printed, ledger-like feel. This serif is the primary brand signature — it separates Slash from every other SaaS fintech that defaults to geometric sans.

inter.$description: UI sans — body, nav, buttons, labels, links, form fields, and the 48px subhead level. The 300 weight appears on 18px body for whisper-quiet secondary copy; 500 dominates for medium-emphasis text and button labels; 600 is reserved for small-caps category labels. Negative letter-spacing tightens at 20px (−0.04em) and loosens as size decreases, characteristic of Inter's optical sizing.
